Why seasonal dishes make the menu better
Fresh ingredients let the kitchen keep the menu interesting and balanced without complicating the dishes.
Seasonal menu
3 min read
Seasonal dishes give the menu a natural rhythm. When ingredients are fresh and in season, the food tastes brighter, the textures are better, and the plating can stay simple.

For guests, seasonal food makes each visit a little different. Familiar dishes stay on the menu, with fresh touches, weekly specials, and local products added.

How to plan a birthday celebration without stress
A simple guide to choosing the space, menu, timing, decor, and service format for a calm birthday.
Events
4 min read
A good birthday starts with a clear format. Before choosing dishes or decor, decide what kind of event it is: calm and family-style, lively with music, or private and elegant.
The next step is the guest count. The hall, seating, menu, serving pace, and timing all depend on it. If you tell the team a rough number early, they can put together a more realistic offer.

Small things make the day easier: arrival time, the cake policy, children's needs, music, decor, and a clear end time. When all of this is agreed in advance, the party goes smoothly for guests and hosts alike.

Why a spa day is a good idea after a busy week
Sauna, hammam, pool, and quiet rest can help guests recover, slow down, and spend peaceful time with family or friends.
Spa and wellness
After a busy week, body and mind often need a slower pace. A spa visit is a simple way to step away from tasks, screens, and daily tension.
Warmth, steam, water, and rest zones create a calm routine. Some guests prefer a dry sauna, others enjoy the softer humidity of a hammam or wet sauna.
A spa day doesn't need to be complicated. A few quiet hours, a convenient time slot, a clean space, and friendly service can turn an ordinary weekend into real rest.

Local cuisine with a modern touch
Traditional dishes can be familiar and still feel fresh when the kitchen respects local flavor and serves them simply and in balance.
Cuisine
Local cuisine often rests on dishes guests already know and love. They don't need reinventing. What matters is serving them with care, in balance, and equally well every time.
A modern touch can be simple: cleaner plating, seasonal garnish, lighter sauces, or better pairing with drinks. These details make familiar food feel renewed without losing its character.
For travelers, local dishes give a sense of place. For regular guests, they are a comfort. A good menu keeps both groups in mind and keeps the flavor honest.

What guests should know before booking a room
Useful details about check-in, breakfast, parking, Wi-Fi, family rooms, and extra services help guests choose the right stay.
Hotel guide
Before booking a room, check the basics: arrival time, check-out time, room type, breakfast, parking, and Wi‑Fi. They decide how comfortable the stay will be.
Guests traveling with family should also ask about extra beds, children’s facilities, quiet rooms, or larger room options. A short conversation before arrival can prevent confusion later.
Extra services make a stay easier: the restaurant, room service, spa, event spaces, or help with a transfer. With them, a plain overnight stay becomes a fuller visit.
